closing.reason: Tried, live in pgpm_prv-archive against MinIO: (1) entry points: archive.configure is the only writer of archive.config (no other insert/update in pgpm_core/pgpm_archive/pgpm_hypertable); every cfg.endpoint reader (to_s3, the tick's chunk PUTs, multipart POST/DELETE, _s3_abort_uploads_at) goes through one of the two signers, both of which now canonicalise the endpoint, so the trailing-slash path is closed on the direct, scheduled and upgraded-row paths. (2) Bucket: the head REFUSES rather than canonicalises a bucket with '/', so 'bucket/', 'bucket/sub', '/bucket' are refused naming p_bucket; both signers and the tick read cfg.bucket raw and identically; a slashed bucket stored by an older install is not rewritten and stays loud (HTTP 400), which the body does not promise otherwise. Uppercase/dotted buckets are accepted (store-specific naming, not this mechanism). (3) Endpoint shapes: port+path+trailing slash canonicalised to 'http://minio:9000/pre/fix'; IPv6 '[::1]:9000/' canonicalised and signed host matches the sent one; uppercase scheme refused (base fails on it too). A percent-encoded dot segment ('/%2E%2E/') is accepted although the body says '..' segments are refused (contrived, not filed). (4) Mutations: only archive_endpoint_trailing_slash_kept alone restores the issue's trailing-slash defect; the other four guard the other refusals, as expected. (5) What survives: V-01. An endpoint spelling the scheme's DEFAULT port ('http://host:80', 'https://<ref>.supabase.co:443/storage/v1/s3', both accepted by configure) is signed with v_host = 'host:80' while libcurl sends 'Host: host' (verified by a listener: it drops a default port), so the store answers 403 SignatureDoesNotMatch to every PUT: reproduced end to end on head and base through a TCP relay on port 80 to MinIO (LIVENESS: the same store spelled without the port exports and lands the object). This is the same signed-host-vs-sent-host mechanism as round 1's userinfo endpoint, which the head now refuses for exactly that reason, and an endpoint 'the signers cannot use' that the PR title says configure refuses. Tier 3 (loud, nothing lost), pre_existing on the PR's surface.
